subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the Externally Set Assignment, who provides the theme and starting points that candidates must respond to?
options: The candidate's own teacher
CCEA, the exam board
A visiting local moderator
The candidate chooses freely
questions.explain: The assignment is 'externally set', meaning the theme and starting points are provided by the exam board (CCEA).

questions.q: The final outcome for the Externally Set Assignment must be produced under which conditions?
options: At home in the candidate's own time
Supervised (controlled) conditions
As a group collaboration
In an open-book online session
questions.explain: The final outcome is completed in a period of supervised time to guarantee it is the candidate's own unaided work.

questions.q: How long is the period of supervised time in which candidates produce the final outcome for the GCSE Externally Set Assignment?
options: 5 hours
8 hours
10 hours
20 hours
questions.explain: Candidates have up to 10 hours of supervised time to complete their final outcome.

questions.q: What must candidates develop before beginning the supervised final-outcome sessions?
options: Preparatory studies
A written examination essay only
Nothing until the supervised time begins
A completed final piece in advance
questions.explain: Candidates produce preparatory work in response to the theme before the supervised sessions.

questions.q: What does the Externally Set Assignment provide to candidates?
options: A finished exemplar piece to copy
A theme with a range of starting points
A single fixed image to reproduce
A written examination with no practical work
questions.explain: The assignment paper offers a theme accompanied by several starting points from which candidates may choose.

questions.q: Assessment Objective AO1 in GCSE Art and Design requires candidates to do what?
options: Present a personal and meaningful final response
Develop ideas through investigations, showing critical understanding of sources
Record ideas and observations as work progresses
Refine work by experimenting with media and techniques
questions.explain: AO1 focuses on developing ideas through investigation and demonstrating critical understanding of sources.

questions.q: During the supervised final-outcome sessions, the work produced must be:
options: The candidate's own unaided work
Completed with direct help from the teacher
A joint effort with classmates
Copied from an approved exemplar
questions.explain: Supervised conditions ensure the final outcome is genuinely the candidate's own unaided work.

questions.q: The preparatory work is completed during which stage of the Externally Set Assignment?
options: The preparatory period before the supervised sessions
The final supervised sessions only
After the final outcome has been submitted
During a written examination
questions.explain: Preparatory studies are developed during the preparatory period leading up to the supervised time.

questions.q: Why does CCEA issue the same theme to all centres for the Externally Set Assignment?
options: To reduce the amount of practical work required
To provide a common, externally controlled basis for fair assessment
To allow candidates to avoid using contextual sources
To make marking optional for teachers
questions.explain: A shared, externally set theme ensures all candidates are assessed fairly against the same starting point.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the preparatory work in the Externally Set Assignment?
options: To replace the need for a final outcome
To develop, explore and refine ideas that lead towards the final outcome
To write an evaluation of another artist's work only
To fill supervised time with unrelated tasks
questions.explain: Preparatory work is where candidates investigate and refine ideas so the final outcome realises their intentions.

questions.q: Why is the final outcome produced under supervised conditions rather than at home?
options: To make the piece quicker to produce
To confirm the final work is authentically the candidate's own
To allow teachers to add finishing touches
To remove the need for preparatory work
questions.explain: Supervision authenticates the final outcome as the candidate's own unaided response.

questions.q: A candidate visits a gallery and photographs artworks linked to the theme. Which assessment objective does recording these observations most directly address?
options: AO3, recording ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions
AO4, presenting a personal and meaningful response
AO2, refining and experimenting with media
None of the assessment objectives
questions.explain: AO3 concerns recording ideas, observations and insights as work progresses.

questions.q: How should the final outcome relate to the preparatory work?
options: It should be unrelated to the preparatory studies
It should realise the intentions developed in the preparatory work
It should copy an artist's piece exactly
It should ignore the set theme
questions.explain: The final outcome should bring together and realise the ideas built up during preparatory work.

questions.q: During the supervised sessions, may candidates refer to their preparatory work?
options: No, all materials must be removed
Yes, they can use their preparatory work to inform the final outcome
Only if the teacher completes it for them
Only if it was made by another candidate
questions.explain: Candidates bring their preparatory studies into the supervised sessions to guide the final outcome.

questions.q: A candidate tries the same design in pencil, ink and collage before deciding on an approach. This best demonstrates which assessment objective?
options: AO1, developing ideas through investigation
AO2, refining work by experimenting with media, materials and techniques
AO3, recording observations
AO4, presenting a personal response
questions.explain: AO2 rewards refining ideas by exploring and experimenting with a range of media and techniques.

questions.q: A candidate has chosen a starting point but has only one rough sketch. What is the most appropriate next step in the preparatory period?
options: Begin the final outcome immediately with no further study
Investigate relevant sources and develop a range of studies and experiments
Discard the starting point and choose a new theme
Wait until the supervised sessions to think about ideas
questions.explain: Strong preparatory work involves investigating sources and producing varied studies before the final outcome.

questions.q: A candidate has 10 hours of supervised time and an ambitious plan. What is the most sensible approach?
options: Attempt far more than can be finished and leave it incomplete
Plan the composition so the outcome can be realised within the supervised time
Complete the piece at home afterwards
Ask a classmate to help finish it
questions.explain: Effective candidates scale their intentions so the final outcome can be completed within the 10 supervised hours.

questions.q: Faced with several starting points on the assignment paper, how should a candidate best choose one?
options: Pick the one that requires the least work
Select the starting point that best suits their ideas, skills and intentions
Choose whichever the teacher completes for them
Respond to every starting point at once
questions.explain: Candidates should choose the starting point that allows them to develop a strong personal response.

questions.q: Which action would be NOT permitted during the supervised final-outcome sessions?
options: Referring to the candidate's own preparatory studies
Receiving direct help from the teacher to complete the work
Working from earlier experiments with media
Continuing to develop ideas planned during preparation
questions.explain: The final outcome must be unaided, so a teacher cannot help produce the work during supervised time.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Art and Design (2017) specification; Component 3: Externally Set Assignment
